h1: Electric Bike Charging Cost per km Calculator
author: ali-ahmad

fields.name: v
fields.label: Battery voltage
fields.hint: Printed on the battery pack or in the bike's manual (common e-bikes and e-scooters use 48 V, 60 V or 72 V packs).

fields.name: ah
fields.label: Battery capacity
fields.hint: Amp hours of the whole pack, from the same label. For a car, enter the pack voltage and Ah, or kWh × 1000 ÷ voltage.

fields.name: range_km
fields.label: Distance on one full charge
fields.hint: Your real range in your riding, not the brochure figure. Riders with a passenger, hills or high speed get less.

fields.name: tariff
fields.label: Electricity rate
fields.hint: Energy rate of your slab from the bill. The default is the Pakistan unprotected rate for 301 to 400 units a month. Enter 0 for charging only from your own daytime solar.

fields.name: eta
fields.label: Charger efficiency
fields.hint: Share of the wall units that ends up in the battery. Leave the default unless you have measured it with a plug-in energy meter.

answer: A {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah electric bike that goes {{in.range_km|int}} km on a charge costs about {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km at {{in.tariff|rs2}} per unit, or {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}} for a full charge of {{out.kwh|2}} units. Units per charge = volts × amp hours ÷ 1000 ÷ charger efficiency; cost per km = units × tariff ÷ km per charge.
how: Battery energy: {{out.v}} V × {{out.ah|1}} Ah ÷ 1000 = the stored units; the charger loses some on the way, so the wall meter counts that ÷ {{out.eta|2}} = {{out.kwh|2}} units for a full charge from empty. Cost of a charge: {{out.kwh|2}} units × {{out.tariff|rs2}} = {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}}. Cost per km: {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}} ÷ {{out.range_km}} km = {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}}.
key_facts: Units to charge an electric bike from empty = battery volts × amp hours ÷ 1000 ÷ charger efficiency; a {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah pack takes about {{out.kwh|2}} units from the wall with a charger at {{d.ebike_charger_eff|pct}} efficiency.

At {{in.tariff|rs2}} per unit, the Pakistan unprotected slab rate for a home using more than {{data.tariff.unprotected.2.upto|int}} and up to {{data.tariff.unprotected.3.upto|int}} units a month, a {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah e-scooter with {{in.range_km|int}} km of range costs about {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km to charge.

A {{ex.1.in.v|int}} V {{ex.1.in.ah|int}} Ah e-scooter that goes {{ex.1.in.range_km|int}} km on a charge costs about {{ex.1.out.rs_per_charge|rs}} per full charge and {{ex.1.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km at the same rate.

Charging from rooftop solar under net billing is not free: each unit you use is a unit you do not export, so its cost is the buyback rate, about {{ex.2.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km for the default bike at {{data.tariff.net_billing.buyback_rs_per_unit_default|rs2}} per unit (a rate not yet notified by NEPRA).

formula.text: Rs per km = (V × Ah ÷ 1000 ÷ η) × tariff ÷ range
lines: V = battery pack voltage; Ah = pack capacity in amp hours
η = charger efficiency (share of wall units that reaches the battery)
V × Ah ÷ 1000 ÷ η = units (kWh) the meter counts for one full charge from empty
tariff = Rs per unit of your slab, or the buyback rate when the units come from your own solar
range = km you really ride on one full charge

sections.h2: Electric bike charging cost per km: the short answer
p: For the default bike, {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km. The figure depends on three things you can read off your own bike and bill: the battery size in volts and amp hours, the real range on a full charge, and the rate per unit you pay. What sets the cost per km is how far each unit takes you, not the battery size; a heavy rider, a passenger or a lot of stop-start riding raises the cost because the same charge covers fewer km.
The calculator counts a full charge from empty. If you top up from half, you pay for half the units; the cost per km stays the same because it is the units per km that matter.

sections.h2: How many units does an e-scooter take to charge?
p: Multiply the pack volts by the amp hours and divide by a thousand for the units stored in the battery, then divide by the charger efficiency for the units the meter counts. The default {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah pack takes {{out.kwh|2}} units from empty; a {{ex.1.in.v|int}} V {{ex.1.in.ah|int}} Ah scooter takes {{ex.1.out.kwh|2}} units.

That is a small share of a home's monthly use, but a scooter charged every day adds {{d.days_per_month|int}} charges a month to the bill. In Pakistan's slab system those extra units can push a home into the next slab, so check the monthly total with the electricity bill calculator before you assume the rate stays the same.

sections.h2: EV charging cost calculator: does it work for an electric car?
p: Yes, the sum is the same for any battery. Enter the car's pack voltage and amp hours (or the kWh × 1000 ÷ volts), its real range and your rate. The example below of a car with a {{ex.3.out.kwh|1}}-unit charge gives {{ex.3.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km at home rates. Public fast chargers bill at their own price per unit, so enter that rate instead of your home tariff.
A car charger at home draws far more power than a scooter charger, so its circuit, cable and breaker must be sized for it by a licensed electrician; the calculator only counts the cost.

On a grid-tied solar system under net billing, a unit used to charge the bike is a unit you would otherwise sell at the buyback rate, so the honest cost is that rate: {{ex.2.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km for the default bike at {{data.tariff.net_billing.buyback_rs_per_unit_default|rs2}} per unit. The buyback rate had not been notified by NEPRA when we last checked, so treat it as an estimate. On an off-grid system with spare daytime power, enter zero.
Charge in daylight to use solar units; a bike plugged in after sunset charges from the grid or from your battery, which costs more.

examples.text: {{out.kwh|2}} units a charge cost {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}} at {{out.tariff|rs2}} per unit. With {{out.range_km|int}} km of range, the cost per km is {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}}: a bigger, faster scooter carries more battery for each km it gives, so it costs more per charge and somewhat more per km.

examples.title: The same bike charged from rooftop solar under net billing
examples.text: Valued at the buyback rate of {{out.tariff|rs2}} per unit you give up by not exporting, a charge of {{out.kwh|2}} units costs {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}}, or {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km. The buyback rate is an estimate until NEPRA notifies it.

examples.title: Electric car charged at home
examples.text: A {{out.v|int}} V {{out.ah|int}} Ah car pack with a home charger at {{out.eta|pct}} takes {{out.kwh|1}} units from empty, {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}} at {{out.tariff|rs2}} per unit. Over {{out.range_km|int}} km of real range that is {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km. Example pack, not a specific car.

mistakes: Using the brochure range. Advertised range is measured light and slow; with a passenger, traffic and hills the real figure is lower, and the cost per km rises in the same proportion.
Forgetting the charger loss. The meter counts more units than the battery stores; dividing by {{d.ebike_charger_eff|pct}} is what turns battery size into units on the bill.

Using the average bill rate for a scooter that pushes the home into a higher slab. The extra units are billed at the rate of the slab you land in, and in an unprotected bill all units move to that rate.
Treating solar charging as free on a net-billing connection. Every unit used is a unit not exported, worth the buyback rate.
safety: Charge with the charger made for your battery, on a sound socket with an earth pin, away from where people sleep and away from flammable items; a damaged or swollen lithium pack can catch fire. A home car charger needs its own circuit, cable and breaker fitted by a licensed electrician.

faq.q: How much does it cost to charge an electric bike in Pakistan?
faq.a: About {{out.rs_per_charge|rs}} for a full charge of a {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah bike at {{in.tariff|rs2}} per unit, or {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km over {{in.range_km|int}} km. Enter your own battery, range and slab rate for your figure.

faq.q: How many units does an electric scooter use per charge?
faq.a: Volts × amp hours ÷ 1000 ÷ charger efficiency: {{out.kwh|2}} units for a {{in.v|int}} V {{in.ah|int}} Ah pack and {{ex.1.out.kwh|2}} units for a {{ex.1.in.v|int}} V {{ex.1.in.ah|int}} Ah pack, from empty.

faq.q: Is an e-bike cheaper to run than a petrol bike?
faq.a: Usually yes on running cost. Petrol cost per km = petrol price per litre ÷ km per litre of your bike; compare that with {{out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km for the default e-bike. Add battery replacement and servicing for a fair long-run comparison.

faq.q: How much does it cost to charge an electric car at home?
faq.a: The same sum with a bigger battery: the example {{ex.3.out.v|int}} V {{ex.3.out.ah|int}} Ah pack takes {{ex.3.out.kwh|1}} units, {{ex.3.out.rs_per_charge|rs}} at {{ex.3.out.tariff|rs2}} per unit, about {{ex.3.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km. Public chargers charge their own rate per unit.

faq.q: Will charging an e-scooter every day raise my electricity slab?
faq.a: It can. Daily charging adds about {{d.days_per_month|int}} charges a month, each of {{out.kwh|2}} units for the default bike. If your home is near a slab limit, run the new monthly total through the electricity bill calculator.

faq.q: What does it cost to charge an e-bike from solar panels?
faq.a: On net billing, value the units at the buyback rate you give up: about {{ex.2.out.rs_per_km|rs2}} per km for the default bike at an estimated {{data.tariff.net_billing.buyback_rs_per_unit_default|rs2}} per unit. Off-grid with spare daytime power, close to nothing.
